facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage trajectory. Carrying-value debt fell from USD 2,849.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 2,413.0 million at 2026-09-30 because the issuer spent cash on a June 2026 tender of USD 406.1 million of 4.0% notes for USD 400.0 million and on third-quarter open-market purchases of USD 32.6 million of principal, while cash fell only from USD 573.0 million to USD 553.4 million, so net debt fell by USD 417.2 million to USD 1,859.6 million. Debt reduction explains 0.82x of the 2.18x fall in reported net leverage and the recovery of trailing reported EBITDA from USD 509.8 million to USD 811.7 million explains 1.36x, mostly because the third-quarter 2025 goodwill impairment of USD 225.7 million left the window. Creditors therefore hold real but smaller protection from debt repaid than the headline ratio suggests. Basis: calculation K3; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue follows light vehicle production in Automotive, housing, energy and data center demand in Industrials, and aerospace, truck and construction cycles in the third segment. Pricing power is limited: the annual report states that customers demand annual price reductions and that raw-material increases have historically been hard to pass on, although the USD 40.8 million of FY2025 tariffs was passed through and design-in positions give some protection. Third-quarter revenue growth was 3.7% in Automotive, 12.6% in Industrials and 13.4% in the third segment, with a USD 24.0 million one-time payment for a cancelled electric vehicle program inside Automotive, so revenue is recurring through platform life but exposed to program cancellations and volume swings, and the credit implication is that earnings can be stable in a flat market and uncertain in a falling one. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Cost of revenue was 70.73% of FY2025 revenue and consists mainly of production materials and employee costs, with research and development at 3.61% and selling, general and administrative expense at 9.62%. Manufacturing sits in lower-cost countries, notably China, Mexico, Malaysia and Bulgaria, which helps margins but ties them to tariffs and currency. Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 22.45% to 22.56% in FY2023 to FY2025, and gross margin was 31.41% in nine months of 2026 against 29.27% in FY2025, but the record holds no organic volume decline, restructuring charges recurred every year, and metals hedges are not accounting hedges, so margin defence under a volume shock rests on cost actions and pass-through that have not been tested at scale. facts.label: Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditure fell from 4.55% of revenue in FY2023 to 3.54% in FY2025 and 2.34% in nine months of 2026, which is 74.46% and 67.09% of depreciation, so part of the cash conversion comes from spending below the asset base's wear, and management expects up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. Free cash flow reached USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months, 71.89% of adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest of USD 157.0 million in FY2025 and a nine-month working-capital inflow of USD 53.1 million that may reverse. Capex flexibility and the option to stop repurchases give room to protect cash over the 2029 to 2032 maturity wall, but the conversion gain is part structural and part timing. facts.label: Competitive forces in credit terms
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate in Automotive, where the company competes with three to four suppliers per application, and sharper in Industrials, where low-cost suppliers in China have entered, which caps pricing and margin. New entrants face high switching costs because customers invest in selecting and testing sensors, but competitors influenced by large vehicle makers limit access to some customers. Substitution risk comes from customers producing in-house and from the shift to electrified platforms, which the electrical protection portfolio partly offsets. Buyers hold the stronger hand through annual price reductions, and suppliers of semiconductors, resins and metals can pass on cost swings that the company has found hard to recover, so the forces most relevant to credit are buyer pricing and input costs acting on margin. facts.label: Policy, macro and technology factors
facts.text: These factors are material to credit and are therefore assessed. Trade policy matters most: tariffs of USD 40.8 million were passed through in FY2025, most Mexican facilities operate under the Maquiladora program whose changes could raise costs, and the February 2026 ruling against certain tariffs leaves potential refunds uncertain and outside guidance. Economic cycles matter through light vehicle production, expected to fall 2% in 2026 on the issuer's cited S&P forecast, and soft U.S. housing in Industrials. Technology cuts both ways: electrification adds high-voltage content, yet slower electric vehicle adoption or cancelled programs, as in the third quarter of 2026, would reduce demand, while data center products, USD 27 million of revenue in 2025 and USD 48 million estimated for 2026, add a small diversifier. facts.label: Credit-translated strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats
facts.text: Strengths are cash-funded deleveraging, free cash flow of USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months, liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million with no maturity before 2029, and customer breadth with no customer above 10% of revenue. Weaknesses are the 53.37% share of segment operating income earned in Automotive, add-backs that were 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025, recurring restructuring and goodwill write-offs, and negative tangible equity. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are growth in data center, aerospace and commercial equipment products, further cash retirement of notes, and an early refinancing of the 2030 notes. Threats are a fall in light vehicle production, loss of tariff pass-through, a return to heavy repurchases or debt-funded acquisitions, and a new internal control weakness. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale is strong, with USD 3,704.5 million of revenue in FY2025 and operations in many countries, and business diversification is average because three segments and a broad customer base spread the business but Automotive still dominates profit. Competitive advantage is average: switching costs protect incumbent positions while customers demand price reductions and low-cost rivals have entered Industrials. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with spending and distributions that can be cut but restructuring that has recurred every year. Margin stability is average because adjusted margins are steady but untested by a volume decline, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion is rising yet helped by capital spending below depreciation and a working-capital inflow. Ability to refinance is average, with BB+ and Ba2 ratings and no maturity before 2029 but 91.39% of notes due in 2030 to 2032 and quarter-end prices below par. Liquidity is strong, and financial policy and governance is average because 2026 behavior favors creditors while capacity for distributions is wide. The trend is improving; the datapoints missing for a firmer view are interim cash interest, a volume downturn, peer benchmarks and the executed financing documents. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 40

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months tailwinds are lower interest, with adjusted net interest expense expected by the issuer at about USD 111 million in 2026 against USD 139 million before its transformation, growth in aerospace, truck and data center markets, and fourth-quarter guidance of USD 942 million to USD 972 million of revenue, 3% to 6% growth, with adjusted operating margin of 19.6% to 19.8%. Headwinds are a 2% fall in 2026 light vehicle production with 4% expected in the fourth quarter, China softness, uncertain tariff refunds, a possible working-capital reversal and capital expenditure of up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. Over three to five years the outlook depends on electrified platform adoption, data center and unmanned aircraft ramps from 2027 and 2028, and the 2029 to 2032 refinancing, where lower leverage helps but market pricing is unknown; no forward model was run, so these items are directional. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a fall in global light vehicle production beyond the 2% the issuer cites, joined by further electric vehicle program cancellations such as the one that produced a USD 24.0 million payment in the third quarter of 2026. The first operational break is lower Automotive volume, where fixed manufacturing costs are absorbed less and customers keep demanding annual price cuts, so margin falls before revenue restructuring cuts costs. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income, so the effect reaches free cash flow quickly, while working capital may reverse the 2026 inflow and tariff refunds are not counted. Liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million, the option to stop repurchases and cut capital expenditure, and no maturity before April 2029 mean the scenario is a leverage and refinancing-cost problem, not a liquidity distress, unless loans and uncollateralized letters of credit on the revolver exceed USD 195.0 million, which would activate the leverage test, or distributions resume. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter revenue below guidance, light vehicle forecast cuts, revolver draws, repurchases and the 2030 refinancing. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Sensata presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, design-in positions and stable adjusted margins, but credit quality is constrained by automotive cyclicality, trade exposure and earnings that rely on large add-backs. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong because free cash flow is rising and capital spending and distributions are flexible. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2030 cluster of notes and revolver, on how note prices move, and on whether management keeps cash-funded deleveraging ahead of shareholder returns. The primary downside path is a fall in automotive volumes that cuts margin and free cash flow while tariff pass-through weakens and distributions resume. Further analysis would require interim cash interest, executed financing documents, peer benchmarks, market yields and a forward model. Top risk: automotive volume and price pressure on a profit base concentrated in one segment. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12

## Request

Source readiness for Sensata Technologies Holding plc as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot, with Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit requested after this module. Scope: whether the eleven supplied documents can support that work, and what stays blocked.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eleven supplied documents support a current credit snapshot of Sensata through the third quarter of 2026, but creditors cannot test their own protections because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied. Covenant, guarantee and security terms rest on the issuer's own summary in the 2025 annual report.

The latest documents are dated 2026-10-27, 22 days before the as-of date, and together they print the statements, debt tables, revolver availability, agency ratings and Adjusted EBITDA the snapshot needs. Financial foundation and Fundamental credit can run on this evidence. Business & governance can run, but ownership and board evidence is thin because the proxy statement was not supplied. Recovery analysis and portfolio fit are not supported, and market pricing is limited to quarter-end fair values of the notes.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sensata's balance sheet is stronger, with net debt at 2.29x LTM reported EBITDA (2.08x adjusted) against 4.47x at year-end 2025, but most of that improvement comes from the 2025 impairment leaving the earnings window rather than from debt repaid.
Basis: calculation K11; calculation K12; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 31; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 34

On adjusted EBITDA the move is smaller, from 2.72x to 2.08x net, and the issuer's own principal-based ratio reads 2.1x. Cash of USD 553.4 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 645.8 million sit against a first note maturity of USD 207.3 million in 2029. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026 interim periods, so interim interest cover is not established; the FY2025 figure is 3.25x.

### Analysis by dimension

Leverage trajectory. Carrying-value debt fell from USD 2,849.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 2,413.0 million at 2026-09-30 because the issuer spent cash on a June 2026 tender of USD 406.1 million of 4.0% notes for USD 400.0 million and on third-quarter open-market purchases of USD 32.6 million of principal, while cash fell only from USD 573.0 million to USD 553.4 million, so net debt fell by USD 417.2 million to USD 1,859.6 million. Debt reduction explains 0.82x of the 2.18x fall in reported net leverage and the recovery of trailing reported EBITDA from USD 509.8 million to USD 811.7 million explains 1.36x, mostly because the third-quarter 2025 goodwill impairment of USD 225.7 million left the window. Creditors therefore hold real but smaller protection from debt repaid than the headline ratio suggests.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

Coverage. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.25x in FY2025 and 2.98x in FY2024, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 5.32x and 5.97x. Interest expense in the first nine months of 2026 was USD 96.8 million against USD 113.4 million a year earlier, which points to better coverage in 2026, but cash interest paid is not printed for interim periods, so the interim ratio is not established and the improvement rests on expense, not cash.
Basis: calculation K15; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 3

Cash flow quality. Operating cash flow was USD 621.5 million in FY2025 and USD 557.8 million in the first nine months of 2026, after USD 131.2 million and USD 68.5 million of capital expenditure, leaving calculated free cash flow of USD 490.3 million and USD 489.3 million. Working capital supplied USD 53.1 million of the 2026 nine-month operating cash flow against an outflow of USD 23.6 million a year earlier, so part of the 2026 cash flow could reverse if receivables and inventory rebuild.
Basis: calculation K6; calculation K23; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Liquidity. Cash of USD 553.4 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 645.8 million, together USD 1,199.2 million or 0.50x total debt, face a debt profile with no maturity before 2029 and a first maturity of USD 207.3 million. Shareholder returns are the main discretionary use: USD 52.4 million of dividends and USD 25.1 million of buybacks in nine months, and the October 2026 dividend would add about USD 17.5 million to net debt.
Basis: calculation K16; calculation K19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14

Data quality and definitions. Reported EBITDA of USD 509.8 million for FY2025 is struck after USD 307.0 million of restructuring-related and other add-backs that include a non-cash goodwill impairment, and the issuer restated its adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 from USD 881.6 million to USD 882.8 million, so adjusted series are comparable only on the later definition. Several printed totals differ from their components by 0.1 through rounding; where the filing itself prints the difference, the total is left unsupplied and logged under the gap lines.
Basis: calculation K14; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

Contrary evidence. The issuer-adjusted view of 2.08x net and strong free cash flow argue that leverage was already moderate before the repayments, and that view wins if add-backs fall as they did from USD 326.1 million in FY2025 to USD 80.2 million over the last twelve months and if working capital inflows persist. Monitoring should watch interim cash interest, any new restructuring add-backs and working capital in the next report.
Basis: calculation K14; calculation K23; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 31

Non-debt funding float and other claims. The sources read show no customer deposits, deferred revenue, factoring or supplier-finance program. Operating lease liabilities of USD 72.8 million at 2025-12-31 and pension obligations of USD 40.4 million at 2026-09-30 sit outside total debt; finance leases of USD 19.8 million are inside it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

- Net cash change for FY2025 is left unsupplied because the filing prints 20.6 as a decrease while the three activity totals and the exchange effect add to a decrease of 20.5 and opening and closing cash differ by 20.7; severity Low; no action closes it short of the issuer's unrounded figures.

- Closing cash for the first nine months of 2025 is left unsupplied because opening cash of 593.7 plus the net change of 197.7 is 791.4 and the filing prints 791.3; severity Low; no action closes it short of unrounded figures.

- Total assets at 2026-09-30 are left unsupplied because total liabilities of 3,619.6 plus total equity of 3,066.8 add to 6,686.4 and the filing prints 6,686.5; severity Low; no action closes it short of unrounded figures.

- The FY2023 balance sheet is not tabulated, so no FY2023 net debt or leverage is stated, and the first and second quarter and half-year income statement and cash flow columns are not tabulated; only EBITDA for those periods is used through the last-twelve-month figures; severity Medium; the action is to add the FY2023 balance sheet from the FY2024 annual report and the 2026 quarterly columns if a longer series is needed.

- Carrying value by note series is not disclosed, only principal by series and one aggregate of premium and deferred financing costs, so the debt instrument table shows principal and a financing cost adjustment row; severity Low; the action is to obtain the per-series carrying amounts.

- The rank and security of finance lease obligations of USD 19.8 million are not stated, so they are excluded from the debt stack and its cumulative leverage; severity Low; the action is to read the lease agreements.

- A floor for the revolver rate is not stated, scheduled principal by year for finance leases is not stated beyond undiscounted payments of USD 3.9 million for 2026, and the finance lease maturity at 2026-09-30 is not stated; severity Low; the action is to read the executed documents and the lease note.

- No restricted-group, guarantor or parent-only statements are supplied for 2025 or 2026, and the credit agreement's covenant ratio is not printed, so leverage is on the plc's consolidated perimeter only; severity Medium; the action is to obtain compliance certificates and the executed credit agreement.

- Adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 and FY2023 was restated by 1.2 and 5.7 against the figures first reported, and the FY2025 add-backs include a non-cash goodwill impairment the issuer does not separate in its reconciliation; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the composition of the add-backs by quarter.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sensata is a widely held public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so creditors face moderate governance risk from shareholder returns and past acquisition write-offs rather than from sponsor extraction.

In 2026 management put debt reduction ahead of shareholder returns, retiring debt with USD 431.8 million of cash in nine months against USD 77.5 million returned to shareholders, and the internal control weaknesses disclosed in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports were remediated by year-end 2025. Risk stays moderate because the credit agreement permits large distributions, the executed documents were not supplied, and USD 375.8 million of Dynapower goodwill was written off in 2024 and 2025.

### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes the sponsor-extraction mechanism but leaves public shareholders as the force behind distributions. Three holders of record, one of them the depository nominee, held the ordinary shares at 2026-01-29, and the proxy statement that would show beneficial holders, related-party dealings and pay incentives was not supplied, so the finding rests on the absence of any sponsor in the filings and not on a holder list.

Shareholder returns have been subordinated to debt reduction since mid-2025 but remain a lever that can be pulled back. Dividends and repurchases took 41.31% of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2025 and 30.73% in FY2025, against 13.89% in the first nine months of 2026, and repurchases fell to USD 25.1 million from USD 120.6 million a year earlier; USD 257.3 million of authorization remains with no expiry date, so a change of priority would not need lender consent within the distribution baskets.
Basis: calculation K9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 30

Liability management has so far favored creditors. Three voluntary purchases between November 2025 and the third quarter of 2026 retired USD 792.7 million of 4.0% note principal for USD 781.8 million of cash, with the revolver undrawn, and the documents describe no exchange, uptier, priming or drop-down; the company does reserve the right to retire or exchange debt in other ways, in amounts that may be material.

Basis: calculation K11; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 39

Legal capacity to move cash out of the borrowing group is wide, but no use beyond ordinary dividends and repurchases is documented, so capacity is a risk and not yet a behavior. As summarized in the annual report, distributions to the parent companies may reach USD 50.0 million a year plus unlimited amounts while senior secured net leverage is at or below 2.5x, 7.0% of market capitalization a year, and the greater of USD 150.0 million and 20.0% of covenant EBITDA, and the credit agreement lets unrestricted subsidiaries be designated, although none has been; these terms rest on the issuer's summary because the executed documents were not supplied.

Reporting quality has been repaired, but the clean record is one year long. Material weaknesses in internal control, disclosed in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports and in quarterly reports through September 2025 and centered on inventory and account reconciliation processes in shared services in Mexico, were declared remediated at 2025-12-31, and the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse for 2024 and unqualified for 2025.

The acquisition record is the main governance concern. Dynapower goodwill of USD 375.8 million was impaired in the third quarters of 2024 and 2025 with USD 4.1 million left, and the Insights Business, impaired by USD 321.7 million in 2023, was sold in 2024 for a purchase price of USD 165.0 million against net assets of about USD 263.4 million; the write-offs are non-cash, but they show that acquisition capital earned less than its cost while management still names acquisitions as an option.
Basis: calculation K12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 96; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7

The business is diversified across three segments with low single-customer concentration, yet it stays tied to the automotive cycle. Automotive was 57.0% of FY2025 revenue, Industrials 21.3% and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment 21.7%, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and the top ten customers have averaged 36 years of relationship; in the third quarter of 2026 Industrials and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment grew 12.6% and 13.4% against 3.7% for Automotive.
Basis: calculation K1; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17

Operating momentum supports debt service, but the third quarter was flattered by a one-time payment. Revenue grew 5.11% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and segment operating income rose to USD 770.0 million from USD 680.3 million; the third quarter included USD 24.0 million from a customer for a cancelled electric vehicle program, so its growth was 7.68% reported and 5.11% without it.
Basis: calculation K5; calculation K6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20

Operations are weighted outside the United States, which adds tariff and trade-policy exposure. Subsidiaries outside the United States earned about 61% of FY2025 revenue, about 20% of it in China, and 92% of employees work outside the United States; the company incurred and passed through USD 40.8 million of tariffs in FY2025, and potential refunds after the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling are uncertain and excluded from fourth-quarter guidance.
Basis: calculation K7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19

Guarantee coverage is thinner than the group's size suggests: the non-U.S. subsidiaries of the borrower were released as guarantors in August 2023, with a conditional duty to reinstate that the documents do not describe, while subsidiaries outside the United States generated about 61% of FY2025 revenue.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a lower risk level is that management reports deleveraging ahead of schedule, ratings are stable at BB+ from S&P and Ba2 from Moody's, internal control now tests as effective, and nothing in the record shows value moving to shareholders at creditors' expense; the level would fall to Low if the executed documents show distribution baskets that tighten as leverage rises and a second clean year-end controls result follows.
Basis: PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 105–107

The strongest case for a higher level is that capacity is wide, shareholders received USD 173.5 million in the first nine months of 2025 before the change of priority, USD 257.3 million of repurchase authorization is unused, and Dynapower shows that acquisitions have lost money; the level would rise to High on a debt-funded acquisition, a return to heavy repurchases while leverage is elevated, the designation of an unrestricted subsidiary, any further guarantee release or non-pro-rata exchange, or a new material weakness in internal control.
Basis: calculation K9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so beneficial holders, board independence, related-party dealings and pay incentives are not established; the finding that no controlling shareholder exists would change if a large holder appears in it.

- The executed credit agreement, indentures and amendments were not supplied, so every statement about distribution, guarantee and unrestricted-subsidiary capacity rests on the issuer's own summary and could change when the baskets, definitions and the 2025 and 2026 amendments are read.
- The purchase price and funding of the Dynapower acquisition are not stated, so the acquisition finding rests on write-offs alone and cannot say whether the original deal was debt funded.
- No lender compliance certificate or basket-usage report was supplied, so the statement that covenants were met is management's, and the distribution-capacity finding cannot be tied to headroom.

- Segment figures are on different bases in the 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports, after products moved between segments, so a shift in business mix between FY2025 and 2026 is not established.

- Management's statement that deleveraging is its top capital allocation priority is an intention and not a commitment, so the moderate risk level would rise if returns to shareholders went back to their 2025 pace.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Sensata Technologies Holding plc
## Request

Fundamental credit for Sensata Technologies Holding plc as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the overall fundamental credit profile, its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside, built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance findings and the filings.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Sensata's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving, as cash-funded debt retirement and rising free cash flow have cut leverage sharply, but automotive cyclicality, tariff exposure and add-back-heavy earnings leave creditors exposed to a volume downturn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Reported net leverage fell from 4.47x at 2025-12-31 to 2.29x at 2026-09-30, or 2.31x pro forma for the quarterly dividend approved in October 2026, and liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million covers the first maturity, in April 2029, 5.78x. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income and 91.39% of note principal falls due in 2030 to 2032, so the profile is adequate and not strong.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

Deleveraging is cash-funded and is the main reason leverage no longer constrains the credit. Carrying-value net debt fell from USD 2,276.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 1,859.6 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 1,877.1 million pro forma for the dividend approved in October 2026, and on adjusted EBITDA net leverage fell from 2.72x to 2.08x, of which debt reduction explains 0.50x and higher earnings 0.14x.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

The sharper fall on reported EBITDA overstates the repair, because the 2025 goodwill impairment left the trailing window: reported net leverage fell 2.18x, of which debt reduction explains 0.82x and the earnings recovery 1.36x, so the adjusted view is the cleaner guide to progress.
Basis: calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Free cash flow is the strongest support and is rising. It was 44.52% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, 58.66% in FY2025 and 71.89% over the last twelve months, or USD 641.2 million, which would repay carrying-value debt in 3.76 years; part of the 2026 gain is a USD 53.1 million working-capital inflow that could reverse.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Liquidity and the maturity profile give a long runway before refinancing matters. Cash was USD 553.4 million at 2026-09-30, with pro forma cash for the dividend approved in October 2026 not established, and the revolver was undrawn at USD 645.8 million, so liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million is 5.78x the USD 207.3 million of notes due in April 2029; the revolver matures on 2030-09-24, weeks after notes due 2030-09-01, so 2030 is the pinch point.
Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

### Limitations

- Cash interest paid is not printed for interim periods, so coverage is judged on interest expense for the last twelve months; the adequate view would weaken if cash interest is materially above expense.

- The 2023 to 2025 record contains no organic volume decline, so margin and cash resilience under a downturn are inferred from adjusted margins and documented cost actions and not observed; the margin finding would change after the first volume decline.
- No peer data or sector benchmark was supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is a judgement from the filings alone and the adequate label has no benchmark.

- Note prices are quarter-end estimates from the filings and no yield or spread was supplied, so the size of the refinancing cost step-up is not established and the refinancing finding could move either way.
- No forward credit model was run, so the outlook rests on one quarter of management guidance and the issuer's own full-year targets; the improving trend is not projected beyond them.

- The proxy statement and executed financing documents were not supplied, so distribution capacity, guarantee coverage and ranking enter this view only as the issuer's own summary and cannot be tested here.

### Company description and credit linkage

Sensata develops, manufactures and sells sensors, electrical protection and power conversion products in three segments, Automotive, Industrials, and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment, which were 57.0%, 21.3% and 21.7% of FY2025 revenue. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue and the top ten customers average 36 years of relationship, which supports cash-flow visibility across platform cycles of five to seven years, but the filings state no order backlog and no contracted volumes, so visibility ends at the platform level and automotive and commercial equipment demand remain cyclical. About 61% of revenue is earned by subsidiaries outside the United States, which adds tariff and currency exposure to debt service. The portfolio has been pruned through the 2024 Insights Business sale, the 2025 sale of the Magnetic Speed and Position Business and the exit from Spear, which cut revenue by 6.5% in FY2025 and left a smaller, more focused earnings base.

### Ownership and group structure

Sensata is a widely held English public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so the sponsor-extraction mechanism is absent but beneficial holdings were not supplied. The plc has no debt of its own: the notes are issued by Sensata Technologies B.V. and Sensata Technologies, Inc., both indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries, and the borrower's distributions to its parents are limited by baskets in the credit agreement. Guarantee coverage is thinner since the August 2023 release of non-U.S. guarantors, and the sponsor and governance risk level is medium because of the acquisition record, wide distribution capacity and a one-year clean internal control record; the executed documents were not supplied, so these terms are the issuer's own summary.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 88–89
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue follows light vehicle production in Automotive, housing, energy and data center demand in Industrials, and aerospace, truck and construction cycles in the third segment. Pricing power is limited: the annual report states that customers demand annual price reductions and that raw-material increases have historically been hard to pass on, although the USD 40.8 million of FY2025 tariffs was passed through and design-in positions give some protection. Third-quarter revenue growth was 3.7% in Automotive, 12.6% in Industrials and 13.4% in the third segment, with a USD 24.0 million one-time payment for a cancelled electric vehicle program inside Automotive, so revenue is recurring through platform life but exposed to program cancellations and volume swings, and the credit implication is that earnings can be stable in a flat market and uncertain in a falling one.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of revenue was 70.73% of FY2025 revenue and consists mainly of production materials and employee costs, with research and development at 3.61% and selling, general and administrative expense at 9.62%. Manufacturing sits in lower-cost countries, notably China, Mexico, Malaysia and Bulgaria, which helps margins but ties them to tariffs and currency. Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 22.45% to 22.56% in FY2023 to FY2025, and gross margin was 31.41% in nine months of 2026 against 29.27% in FY2025, but the record holds no organic volume decline, restructuring charges recurred every year, and metals hedges are not accounting hedges, so margin defence under a volume shock rests on cost actions and pass-through that have not been tested at scale.

Capital expenditure fell from 4.55% of revenue in FY2023 to 3.54% in FY2025 and 2.34% in nine months of 2026, which is 74.46% and 67.09% of depreciation, so part of the cash conversion comes from spending below the asset base's wear, and management expects up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. ### Competitive forces in credit terms

Rivalry is moderate in Automotive, where the company competes with three to four suppliers per application, and sharper in Industrials, where low-cost suppliers in China have entered, which caps pricing and margin. New entrants face high switching costs because customers invest in selecting and testing sensors, but competitors influenced by large vehicle makers limit access to some customers. Substitution risk comes from customers producing in-house and from the shift to electrified platforms, which the electrical protection portfolio partly offsets. Buyers hold the stronger hand through annual price reductions, and suppliers of semiconductors, resins and metals can pass on cost swings that the company has found hard to recover, so the forces most relevant to credit are buyer pricing and input costs acting on margin.
### Policy, macro and technology factors

These factors are material to credit and are therefore assessed. Trade policy matters most: tariffs of USD 40.8 million were passed through in FY2025, most Mexican facilities operate under the Maquiladora program whose changes could raise costs, and the February 2026 ruling against certain tariffs leaves potential refunds uncertain and outside guidance. Economic cycles matter through light vehicle production, expected to fall 2% in 2026 on the issuer's cited S&P forecast, and soft U.S. housing in Industrials. Technology cuts both ways: electrification adds high-voltage content, yet slower electric vehicle adoption or cancelled programs, as in the third quarter of 2026, would reduce demand, while data center products, USD 27 million of revenue in 2025 and USD 48 million estimated for 2026, add a small diversifier.

### Credit-translated strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats

Strengths are cash-funded deleveraging, free cash flow of USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months, liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million with no maturity before 2029, and customer breadth with no customer above 10% of revenue. Weaknesses are the 53.37% share of segment operating income earned in Automotive, add-backs that were 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025, recurring restructuring and goodwill write-offs, and negative tangible equity. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are growth in data center, aerospace and commercial equipment products, further cash retirement of notes, and an early refinancing of the 2030 notes. Threats are a fall in light vehicle production, loss of tariff pass-through, a return to heavy repurchases or debt-funded acquisitions, and a new internal control weakness.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is strong, with USD 3,704.5 million of revenue in FY2025 and operations in many countries, and business diversification is average because three segments and a broad customer base spread the business but Automotive still dominates profit. Competitive advantage is average: switching costs protect incumbent positions while customers demand price reductions and low-cost rivals have entered Industrials. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with spending and distributions that can be cut but restructuring that has recurred every year. Margin stability is average because adjusted margins are steady but untested by a volume decline, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion is rising yet helped by capital spending below depreciation and a working-capital inflow. Ability to refinance is average, with BB+ and Ba2 ratings and no maturity before 2029 but 91.39% of notes due in 2030 to 2032 and quarter-end prices below par. Liquidity is strong, and financial policy and governance is average because 2026 behavior favors creditors while capacity for distributions is wide. The trend is improving; the datapoints missing for a firmer view are interim cash interest, a volume downturn, peer benchmarks and the executed financing documents.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months tailwinds are lower interest, with adjusted net interest expense expected by the issuer at about USD 111 million in 2026 against USD 139 million before its transformation, growth in aerospace, truck and data center markets, and fourth-quarter guidance of USD 942 million to USD 972 million of revenue, 3% to 6% growth, with adjusted operating margin of 19.6% to 19.8%. Headwinds are a 2% fall in 2026 light vehicle production with 4% expected in the fourth quarter, China softness, uncertain tariff refunds, a possible working-capital reversal and capital expenditure of up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. Over three to five years the outlook depends on electrified platform adoption, data center and unmanned aircraft ramps from 2027 and 2028, and the 2029 to 2032 refinancing, where lower leverage helps but market pricing is unknown; no forward model was run, so these items are directional.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a fall in global light vehicle production beyond the 2% the issuer cites, joined by further electric vehicle program cancellations such as the one that produced a USD 24.0 million payment in the third quarter of 2026. The first operational break is lower Automotive volume, where fixed manufacturing costs are absorbed less and customers keep demanding annual price cuts, so margin falls before revenue restructuring cuts costs. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income, so the effect reaches free cash flow quickly, while working capital may reverse the 2026 inflow and tariff refunds are not counted. Liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million, the option to stop repurchases and cut capital expenditure, and no maturity before April 2029 mean the scenario is a leverage and refinancing-cost problem, not a liquidity distress, unless loans and uncollateralized letters of credit on the revolver exceed USD 195.0 million, which would activate the leverage test, or distributions resume. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter revenue below guidance, light vehicle forecast cuts, revolver draws, repurchases and the 2030 refinancing.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Sensata presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, design-in positions and stable adjusted margins, but credit quality is constrained by automotive cyclicality, trade exposure and earnings that rely on large add-backs. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong because free cash flow is rising and capital spending and distributions are flexible. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2030 cluster of notes and revolver, on how note prices move, and on whether management keeps cash-funded deleveraging ahead of shareholder returns. The primary downside path is a fall in automotive volumes that cuts margin and free cash flow while tariff pass-through weakens and distributions resume. Further analysis would require interim cash interest, executed financing documents, peer benchmarks, market yields and a forward model. Top risk: automotive volume and price pressure on a profit base concentrated in one segment.

## Gaps

- Cash interest paid and cash taxes paid are not printed for interim periods, so interest coverage for the last twelve months is on interest expense; severity Medium; the action is to obtain interim cash flow supplements.

- No peer or sector benchmark was supplied, so the business and financial profile is not compared with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector; severity Medium; the action is to run the peer benchmark.

- No volume downturn sits in the FY2023 to FY2025 record, so margin and cash resilience under stress are not observed; severity Medium; the action is to obtain a longer history with a cycle low and to run the downside analysis.

- No yield, spread or trade price for the notes was supplied beyond quarter-end estimates, so the cost of refinancing the 2030 to 2032 maturities is not established; severity Medium; the action is to obtain market data.
- No forward credit model was run, so the outlook is limited to guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026 and the issuer's own targets; severity Medium; the action is to run the forward credit model.

- The composition of add-backs by quarter, other than the goodwill impairment, is not supplied, so recurring restructuring cash cost is not isolated; severity Medium; the action is to obtain the quarterly add-back detail.

- The executed credit agreement, indentures and proxy statement were not supplied, so distribution capacity, guarantee coverage, ranking and ownership concentration are not tested; severity High; the action is to obtain them and run the legal and covenant analysis.

- No order backlog, contract duration or end-market revenue split beyond the three segments is stated, so revenue visibility rests on design-in statements; severity Low; the action is to ask the issuer.
- Pension, operating lease, hedging and foreign-exchange exposures were not analysed here; severity Low; the action is to run the rates, currency and hedging analysis.
- The earnings changes analysis was not run, so first- and second-quarter drivers are not tabulated; severity Low; the action is to run it.
